team: JAKIROVIC: “WE SAW THEIR PROBLEMS!”  Hull City
quote_text:
Sergej, Hull City's first-ever league win in the  Premier League against Manchester United. How do  
you feel? They told me. No, I didn't know about  this information. I feel excellent and I'm very  
happy because of our players. They put everything  on the pitch today. What we agreed in the meeting  
all this week, what we tried to practise there,  and this is the result in the end. I'm very,  
very pleased with them. And you scored two  big goals at crucial times in that first  
half this afternoon. Yeah, we tried something  on Friday, so we had some plan there to try to  
punish them with how they stand, especially on  wide free-kicks, to make some blocks there. And  
Nobel scored, and Semi, of course. Home form is  always so important for teams coming up in the  
Premier League. To get that first win, to get a  clean sheet, that should give you, the supporters  
and everybody here a huge amount of confidence  going forward. A big boost for us for the future.  
Like I spoke all last week about the possibility  that we can win, this is maybe the key because  
I have to convince my players that we are capable  of playing at this level. We showed last season  
that we are very strong, very mentally strong,  and that we can compete against everyone. This  
is maybe the key, and they showed it today on the  pitch. What's the situation with Nobel and Semi?  
Obviously, they came off with problems. That  was not the plan. We had four substitutions  
in the defensive line. I don't know. After  the medical check, I will know much more,  
but right now I don't know. Semi is complaining  about his hamstring and Nobel about his adductor.  
How concerned are you, given the injury problems  you've got here? Maybe we will bring some new  
players again. We have 10 days to go, so we will  see. It depends on their problems. Hidemasa,  
you said he might be on the bench today. What's  the situation with him? Can we see him at Stoke?  
No, he had training today. It was better for him  and he will be in the squad for Stoke. Any other  
concerns injury-wise? No, Coyle, always with  his ankle, so that is normal. Transfer-wise,  
what can we expect in the next couple of days? Are  you close to anything? Obviously, we know García  
was close. Is that still happening, or...? Two  strikers, two wingers, one or two midfielders. It  
depends now on the defensive line, so it will be  busy. You've obviously got no strikers apart from  
McBurnie, aside from young Sellars-Fleming. What  are you going to do at Stoke? How many changes can  
we expect? For the next game, or...? The League  Cup game on Tuesday. We will see on Monday who is  
alive. We will see. Sergej, it looked a lot like  many of the games last season. How important,  
as you bring new players in, is it that you don't  lose all the good things about last season? It's  
very important because it's about the team. I had  conversations with our main players, I can say,  
the leaders, and we need as soon as possible  to create togetherness in our dressing room.  
Some of them speak good English and some don't  speak so well. We will try, but this victory is  
amazing because now they are convinced that they  can compete at this level and should continue like  
this. You could have given more debuts today,  but are you trying to do it gradually and get  
people used to the way of playing? We have a  training session every day, so we are trying  
everything on the pitch. After training,  we analyse everything about the principles.  
We also had a plan today to put Jens or Gourna  there, but because of injuries I couldn't do  
that. They will get a chance on Tuesday. Are you  concerned about all these injuries and the causes  
behind them, like last season? Yes, exactly. I  remember the game on December 29 when we played  
Middlesbrough away. We had 12 players. We have  an Under-21 team, so maybe we will use some of  
them. Is this something the club has looked at?  Why are you getting so many injuries? These are  
some old problems from last season. This is a  contact sport, so every challenge, every duel,  
there is a possibility that you will get injured.  We can't sign 50 players. We can only register 25.  
You mentioned noticing something about Manchester  United's set-piece setup that you looked at. What  
was that? It obviously worked. This is a secret.  This is a secret. Come on, tell us. I don't have  
a coach just for set pieces. Marko, Anđelo, my  assistant coach and Holden, they are doing this.  
This is our secret. How did you go from a back  four to a back five? I know you played that last  
season, but why was that the particular choice  today? Because Man United come very, very high  
with Shaw. Luke Shaw also tries to overload the  midfield. Our main task was to close these gaps  
between the lines, and when we steal the ball, to  be very vertical and very quick. Also, in those  
transitions, we tried to switch the side because  our wing-backs were completely alone, and then  
have numbers in the box. I think we had two very  good chances after this. We also didn't allow any  
one-on-one or 100 per cent chance for Man United.  Did you expect more from Manchester United in  
terms of a response? This is a tricky question.  No, no, no. This is a tricky question. I can speak  
only about my team because I always care about  my team. Of course, we watched Man United three  
times, once live, and we saw their problems.  Then we tried to use this today. Regan Slater  
has been with the club for a long time. I think  he cost £50,000. What can you say? £50,000, not  
bad. Fully deserved. When I arrived here, Regan  Slater was not a first-team player. I think he  
came on against Preston at home at half-time.  He completely turned the game, and since then  
he's been a first-11 player. He's my first  choice, always, and I like him a lot because  
every training session and every game, he's 100  per cent. How proud are you of the players? You  
could have brought in more debutants and more  new signings, but you stuck with the core that  
got you here. You mean eight players from last  season? This is our spine. We know each other.  
We have been together for one year, so they know  everything. Sometimes I don't even need to speak  
with them. When I just look at Ryan Giles, for  example, he knows everything, what I mean and what  
I'm thinking. Tzolakis, Mendy and Elliot, this is  normal, our normal choice. Of course, we have some  
new players there, but for tactical reasons they  didn't play today. On Tuesday, they will play.  
Sergej, can I ask you about your goalkeeper? He's  obviously going to play a huge part if you stay  
up this season. He seemed very impressive on  his debut, especially with the physicality of  
the Premier League. How happy were you with  his debut? Very happy. That's why we bought  
him and spent some money there. He's a Greece  international and an Olympiacos player. If you  
follow Greek football, Olympiacos is a huge stress  and huge pressure. He's used to this. For him,  
I think this is like a cup of tea because  Olympiacos is a very big club in Greece, and I'm  
very happy with him. Also with Jack Butland, who  had an injury, and with Dillon. We have three very  
good goalkeepers. What do you think that does for  the defence? When you bring in someone like Mendy,  
who's just 21 years old, and you have a goalkeeper  of that pedigree performing well behind him? Mendy  
also has a lot of experience at this level because  he played in Primera. He played in a Conference  
League final. He's 21 years old, so it's big  experience for him. Since the first game,  
he has played like he has been with us for one  year. How big a statement win is this after all  
the criticism and noise before the game? Before  the start of the season, for me, it's normal. I  
don't have any problems with critics or opinions.  These are their opinions. Like I said in another  
press conference, we tried to prove them wrong,  and today we won the game. Now there are 37 to go,  
so we will try to continue like this. Yes, first  win. Yes, 100 per cent efficiency. Good. I'm very,  
very happy because of all the people in the  club. Sergej, just one quick one. What can  
this do for you in the transfer market, for  players who are perhaps unsure about whether  
you're serious? Obviously, everybody is saying  you're going to get relegated. To go and play  
like that and get a result, do you think that  can help you in the final week? They will come  
100 per cent now. I don't have any doubts. Really?  Yeah, 100 per cent. Are you expecting a rush like  
last season? I was in a similar position last  season. I tried to explain to some people. Some  
players chose other clubs, and then they joined us  in January, if you remember. Yes, they will come.
